chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn al-Hukam narrated to me, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Rizqi, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them.

He said: For the Fire there are seven gates: A gate through which Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun enter; a gate through which polytheists and disbelievers enter, from those who did not believe in God for even a twinkling of an eye; a gate through which the Banu Umayya enter, which is exclusive to them, no one jostles them in it, and it is the Gate of Luza, it is the Gate of Saqar, and it is the Gate of the Abyss, which casts them down for seventy autumns. And whenever it casts them down for seventy autumns, a surge lifts them up and throws them to its highest part for seventy autumns, then it casts them down again for seventy autumns, so they remain thus forever, abiding eternally; and a gate through which our enemies, those who fought us, and those who abandoned us enter. And indeed, it is the greatest of the gates and the most intense in heat.

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Rizqi said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The gate you mentioned from your father from your grandfather (peace be upon them) that the Banu Umayya enter through it, does it enter those who died among them upon polytheism, or those among them who attained Islam? He said: May you lose your mother! Did you not hear him say: 'And a gate through which polytheists and disbelievers enter'? This gate enters every polytheist and every disbeliever who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning. And this other gate enters the Banu Umayya, for it is exclusive to Abu Sufyan, Muawiyah, and the household of Marwan. They enter through that gate, and the Fire breaks them with a breaking in which you do not hear their groaning, and they neither live nor die in it.

key_terms.أَبُو سُفْيَانَ وَمُعَاوِيَةَ وَآلِ مَرْ: Abu Sufyan, Muawiyah, and the household of Marwan

ai.seo_question: What are the seven gates of Hell according to Shia hadith and who enters each?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the unique eschatological status of the Banu Umayya, specifying that their gate (Saqar) is exclusive to the Umayyad lineage—Abu Sufyan, Muawiyah, and the Marwanids—regardless of their individual faith status. This exclusivity underscores the Shia doctrine of *Walayah* (divine authority), where enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt constitutes a distinct category of damnation separate from general polytheism or disbelief.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-52 Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qat’tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hikam, on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Fazeel al-Rizqi, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB),

“There are seven gates for Hell. One gate is for Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun (Korah) to enter. The second gate is for the polytheists and the atheists to enter Hell who did not believe in God even for the twinkling of an eye. The third gate is especially for the Umayyad clan to enter. No one else will be there. That is the blazing gate. It is the burning gate. It is the swallowing gate which takes them into a depth of seventy Kharives each of which equals eighty years. It pulls them down into the depth of Hell. Once in the depth of Hell there shall be a big smoldering in Hell and they will be thrown back the same distance. This will be repeated continuously and they shall abide therein forever. The fourth gate is especially for our enemies; those who fought with us and those who refused to help us. This gate is the greatest of all and it is the most aflame.”

Muhammad ibn al-Fazeel al-Rizqi added, “I told Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), ‘Is the gate which you quoted your father on the authority of your grandfather as saying that the Umayyads shall enter meant for those who died as atheists or does it also include those of the Umayyads who accepted Islam?’ The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘O may you lose your mother! Did you not hear that there is an especial gate for the atheists and the polytheists to enter! This gate is for every atheist and polytheist who doesn’t believe in the Resurrection Day and the Reckoning of Deeds. However, there is an especial gate for the Umayyad clan to enter. That gate belongs to Abu Sufyan, Muawiyah and the household of Marvan. They shall enter Hell from that gate and they shall be tortured by its fire such that they cannot breathe. In fact, they are neither dead nor alive there.”
